1206 ACCOUNT
Synlett 2001, No. 8, 1206–1213 ISSN 0936-5214 © Thieme Stuttgart · New York
An Efficient New Methodology for the Synthesis of 1-Functionalized 2-Halo-2-
alkenes via Hydrohalogenation Reaction of Electron-Deficient Allenes
Shengming Ma,* Lintao Li
State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai 
200032, P. R. China
Fax +86-21-64166128; E-mail: masm@pub.sioc.ac.cn
Received 4 April 2001
Abstract: The hydrohalogenation reactions of electron-deficient al-
lenes, such as 1,2-allenic ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amides,
nitriles, sulfoxides (with the use of AlX3/H2O), sulfones, and phos-
phine oxides with MX (X = I, Br, Cl, M = Na, Li) in different sol-
vents, such as HOAc, CF3COOH-HOAc (1:1), CF3COOH and THF
were studied. The reaction is nucleophilic conjugate addition in na-
ture and provides efficient entries to 1-functionalized 2-halo-2-alk-
enes. The /c98/c44/c103- over /c97/c44/c98-selectivity and stereoselectivity depend on
the solvent(s) and the temperature applied. In most cases, the Z- and
E-isomers can be easily separated with chromatography on silica
gel. The subsequent cross coupling reaction with organometallic re-
agents and terminal alkynes showed the synthetic potential of these
products.
1 Introduction
2 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic Ketones
3 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic Carboxylic
Acids
4 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic Carboxylates
5 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 2,3-Dienamides
6 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 2,3-Dienenitriles
7 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic Sulfones
8 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic Sulfoxides
9 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic
Diphenylphosphine Oxides
10 Synthetic Application
11 Conclusion
Key words: electron-deficient allenes, hydrohalogenation, regiose-
lectivity, stereoselectivity, solvent effect
1 Introduction
1-Functionalized 2-halo-2-alkenes are classes of com-
pounds with synthetic importance due to the uniquely lo-
cated carbon-carbon double bonds. Allenes have been
found to have high and unique reactivities, due to the ex-
istence of the two orthogonal 
/c112-bonds.1 During the course
of our study on the  chemistry of allene, 2 we rationalized
from the retrosynthetic analysis that the hydrohalogena-
tion reaction of electron-deficient allenes would be one of
the most efficient ways for the synthesis of 
/c98-halogen sub-
stituted /c98/c44/c103/c45unsaturated products (equation 1). Since the
hydrohalogenation of electron-deficient alkynes afforded
1-functionalized 2-halo-1-alkenes, 3 a challenge encoun-
tered here would be the potential migration of the C=C
bond from the 
/c98,/c103-position to the /c97,/c98-position, thus, af-
fording a synthetically useless mixture of /c98/c44/c103/c45unsaturated
products and /c97/c44/c98/c45unsaturated products.4 We have devel-
oped the hydrohalogenation reaction of a varieties of elec-
tron-deficient allenes, such as 1,2-allenic ketones,
carboxylic acids, esters, amides, nitriles, sulfoxides (with
the use of AlX
3/H2O), sulfones, and phosphine oxides
with MX in HOAc, CF 3COOH-HOAc, CF 3COOH or
THF to afford 1-functionalized 2-halo-2-alkenes. Here,
the reaction medium is the key to avoid the formation of a
mixture of 
/c98/c44/c103/c45unsaturated and /c97/c44/c98/c45unsaturated prod-
ucts.
Equation 1
2 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic 
Ketones
Hydrochlorination reaction of 1,2-allenyl ketones by HCl
was reported to lead to polymerization, while hydrochlo-
rination using N,N’-dimethylhydrazine dihydrochloride
or SnCl
4 afforded a mixture of /c98/c44/c103-unsaturated and /c97/c44/c98-
unsaturated /c98-chloroenones, majoring the /c97/c44/c98-enones.5
We found that reaction of 3,4-pentadien-2-one with NaI,
LiI, LiBrH
2O, and LiClH2O in acetic acid at 25 °C af-
forded the corresponding 4-halo-4-penten-2-one with
yields ranging from 69% to 82% (equation 2).
6 Under dif-
ferent reaction conditions, the reaction of 3,4-pentadien-
2-one with LiI or NaI afforded different ratio of 
/c98/c44/c103-unsat-
urated enone 1 / /c97/c44/c98-unsaturated enone 2. Reaction of 3,4-
pentadien-2-one with NaI in acetic acid at 25 °C afforded
the mixture of /c98/c44/c103-unsaturated enone 1 and /c97/c44/c98-unsaturat-
ed enone 2 with a ratio of 91:9. The reaction can also oc-
cur in a 1:1 mixture of HOAc and THF, but the ratio of
/c98/c44/c103-unsaturated enone  1 / /c97/c44/c98-unsaturated enone 2 is
87:13, while in a solution of HOAc (3 equiv.) in THF at a
lower reaction temperature the selectivity of the reaction

Typical Procedure for a Larger Scale Preparation
Synthesis of 4-Bromo-3-penten-2-one :8 A three-necked,
round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic stirring
bar, an addition funnel, a thermometer, and a reflux con-
denser was flushed with nitrogen and charged with 132 g
(0.5 mol) of triphenylphosphine and 400 mL of dichlo-
romethane. The flask was cooled with an ice-water bath,
and a solution of 80 g (0.5 mol) of bromine in 50 mL of
dichloromethane was added dropwise so that the temper-
ature of the mixture did not rise above 10 °C. After the ad-
dition was over, a solution of 50 g (0.5 mol) of
acetylacetone in 50 mL of dichloromethane was added
dropwise within 10 min at room temperature. The mixture
was then heated under reflux for 4-5 h with stirring until
the evolution of hydrogen bromide ceased. The cooled
mixture was concentrated using a rotary evaporator. 500
mL of ether was added to the residue and triphenylphos-
phine oxide was precipitated. The resulting precipitate
was removed by suction and washed with ether (2
/c180100
mL). The filtrate and washings were combined and evap-
orated. Distillation of the residue under reduced pressure
gave 70 g (85%) of 4-bromo-3-penten-2-one; bp 54-
55 °C/15 mmHg.
 Synthesis of 3,4-Pentadien-2-one :
8 A dry 500 mL three-
necked round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic
stirring bar and an addition funnel, was charged with 65 g
(0.40 mol) of 4-bromo-3-penten-2-one and 250 mL of an-
hydrous ether. To this mixture was added a solution of 45
g (0.44 mol) of triethylamine in 40 mL of ether dropwise
at room temperature. After the mixture was stirred for 5 h
at r.t., the precipitate of triethylamine hydrobromide was
removed by suction and washed with ether (2
/c180100 mL).
The combined ether solution was washed with 5% hydro-
chloric acid. The solution was then washed with cold wa-
ter (50 mL) and dried with magnesium sulfate.
Evaporation and distillation afforded 21.5 g (65%) of 3,4-
pentadien-2-one; bp 50 °C/60 mmHg.

moved to Shanghai Institute

nese Academy of Sciences
and works there as a re-
search associate under th

search interest is the deve l-
opment of new synthet ic
methodologies.
Shengming Ma was born in
Zhejiang Province (P. R.
China) in 1965. He obtained
his bachelor’s degree at
Hangzhou University in
1986. He then moved to
Shanghai Institute of Organ-

Academy of Sciences as a
graduate student, and ob-
tained his Ph.D. degree
there in 1990 under the su-

same institute as a Research

joined Professor Venanzi’s

He returned to Shanghai In-

Research Professor and Di-

Chemistry, Shanghai Insti-

Chinese Academy of Sci-
ences. His research interests
are focused on development
of new methodologies with
an emphasis on OMCOS
chemistry, especially asym-
metric synthesis and the
ir

Synthesis of 4-Iodo-4-penten-2-one :7 A 250 mL three-
necked round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic
stirring bar, an addition funnel, and a thermometer was
charged with 24.3 g (0.16 mol) of lithium iodide, 23.4 g
(0.39 mol) of acetic acid and 150 mL of tetrahydrofuran,
and flushed with nitrogen. The flask was cooled with an
ice-water bath and a solution of 10.7 g (0.13 mol) of 3,4-
pentadien-2-one in 50 mL of tetrahydrofuran was added
so that the temperature of the mixture did not rise above
0 °C. After stirring at 0 °C for 
/c1268 h, the reaction mixture
was evaporated, diluted with ether (250 mL), carefully
neutralized with cool aqueous K
2CO3. The two phases
were separated and the aqueous layer was extracted with
ether (2
/c180100 mL). The combined organic layers were
washed with saturated brine (3 /c180100 mL) and dried over
magnesium sulfate. Evaporation and distillation afforded
4-iodo-4-penten-2-one. Yield 16.9 g (62%), bp 62 °C/1
mmHg.
The hydroiodination and hydr obromination reactions of
3-alkyl-1,2-allenyl ketones with MX in HOAc at 25 °C
yielded Z-isomer, i.e. Z-3, in high yield with fairly good
stereoselectivity, although the corresponding hydrochlori-
nation reaction afforded the products E-3 and Z-3 with
lower stereoselectivities (Scheme 1). The formation of
/c97/c44/c98-unsaturated /c98-haloenones was not observed.7
Scheme 1
Hydrohalogenation reaction of 5-methyl-3,4-hexadien-2-
one with NaI, LiBrH
2O, and LiClH2O in acetic acid at
25 °C also went smoothly to afford 4-halo-5-methyl-4-
hexen-2-ones in high yields (equation 3). The /c98/c44/c103 carbon-
carbon double bonds of 4 are stabilized by the four substit-
uents, thus, the formation of /c97/c44/c98/c45unsaturated enones was
not observed.7
Hydrohalogenation reaction of 3-methyl-3,4-pentadien-2-
one with NaI in HOAc afforded a mixture of 
/c98/c44/c103-unsatur-
ated /c98-iodoenone 5a and /c97/c44/c98-unsaturated /c98-iodoenone 6a
with an uninteresting ratio of 31:69. The corresponding
reaction in CF
3COOH afforded 5a highly selectively, al-
beit in low yield (5a: 6a = 96:4, 25%). Using a 3 equiv so-
lution of CF 3COOH in THF as the solvent greatly
improved the yields, but the ratios of 5a/6a still need op-
timization (78%, 80:20). Finally we found that the reac-
tion could afford the 
/c98/c44/c103-unsaturated /c98/c45iodoenone 5a
highly selectively when the reaction was carried out in a
1:1 mixture of CF
3COOH and HOAc (82%, 5a:
6a = 96:4). Under these conditions, 3-methyl-3,4-pentadi-
en-2-one or 3-butyl-3,4-pentadien-2-one reacted smooth-
ly with NaI, LiBr-H
2O, and LiCl-H 2O to afford the
corresponding 4-halo-3-methyl(or butyl)-4-penten-2-
ones 5 in high yields (70-99%) with high selectivity over
the 
/c97,/c98-unsaturated enones 6 (2-5%) (equation 4).7
Equation 4
3 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic 
Carboxylic Acids
Reaction of 2,3-butadienoic acid with NaI, LiBr-H2O, and
LiCl-H2O in HOAc at 70 °C afforded the corresponding
3-halo-3-butadienoic acid with yields ranging from 87-
92%.
6 
Hydroiodination reaction of 4-alkyl substituted 2,3-buta-
dienoic acid with NaI in HOAc under reflux afforded Z-
isomer of 3-halo-3-alkenoic acid with fairly good stereo-
selectivity. The corresponding reaction with LiBrH
2O or
LiClH2O afforded a mixture of the products Z-7 and E-7
with low selectivities  (Scheme 2). Products Z-7 and E-7
can be separated by column chromatography on silica gel.
9
The hydrohalogenation reaction of 2-methyl-substituted
2,3-butadienoic acid with MX (M = Li, Na) in CF
3CO2H
afforded the corresponding products in good yields
(Scheme 3).

4 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic 
Carboxylates
Hydrohalogenation reaction of unsubstituted methyl 2,3-
butadienoate with MX in HOAc afforded methyl 3-halo-
3-butenoates with yields ranging from 56-86%.
6
The reaction of ethyl 4-alkyl substituted 2,3-alkadienoates
with NaI, LiBr-H
2O, and LiCl-H2O in HOAc or CF3CO2H
went smoothly and afforded the corresponding ethyl
3-halo-3-alkenoates in high yields (70-98%), but the ste-
reoselectivity is not high (equation 5).
9 However, a major
side reaction, i.e., the hydrolysis of the ester group to car-
boxylic acid, was observed when ethyl 2,3-pentadienoate
was treated with HX.
10 It afforded a mixture of ethyl
3-halo-3-pentenoate together with 3-halo-3-pentenoic
acid (equation 6).9 
Equation 5
Equation 6
Hydrohalogenation reaction of ethyl 2-methyl-2,3-butadi-
enoate with MX in HOAc afforded a mixture of 2-enoates
12a and 3-enoates 11a in low yields and selectivities
(Yields of 12a and 11a : NaI: 10%, 41%; LiBr: <5%,
<5%). However, when a 1:1 mixture of CF
3CO2H and
HOAc or CF3CO2H alone was used as the reaction medi-
um, the hydrohalogenation went smoothly to afford ethyl
3-halo-2-methyl-3-butenoates 11a in very good yields
(80-95%) and the formation of 2-enoates 12a was not ob-
served. The corresponding reaction with HX was reported
to afford a mixture of 
/c98,/c103-unsaturated alkenoate and /c97/c44/c98-
unsaturated alkenoate. 11 The reaction in CF 3CO2H was
much more efficient than that in CF 3CO2H-HOAc (1:1).
Under the reaction conditions the hydrohalogenation re-
action of ethyl 2-propyl-2,3-butadienoate also afforded
ethyl 3-halo-2-propyl-3-butenoates in fairly good yields
(63-98%)  and  the  formation of 2-enoates 12b was not
observed (equation 7).
12

action also went smoothly to afford the corresponding
/c98,/c103-unsaturated 3-enoates 14 (Scheme 4) with yields
ranging from 55% to 89%.

5 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 2,3-Diena-
mides
Hydrohalogenation reaction of 2,3-dienamide 16 usually
afforded the corresponding 3-halo-3-alkenamides in high
yields. Both MX-HOAc, MX-CF
3CO2H and aqueous HX
systems can be applied. Hydrohalogenation reaction of
4-methyl-2,3-pentadienamide 16a or 2,3-butadienamide
16c with NaI, LiBrH2O, and LiClH2O in HOAc at 70 °C
afforded the corresponding 3-halo-3-alkenamide 17 with
yields ranging from 75% to 99%. Hydrohalogenation re-
action of 2,3-octadienamide 16b with MX in HOAc or
CF
3CO2H at 70 °C afforded the corresponding 3-halo-3-
octenamides 17 in high yields (69-98%) with low stereo-
selectivities. Both MX-CF 3CO2H and aqueous HX sys-
tems can be applied to N-benzyl 2-methyl-2,3-
butadienamide (16d) (Scheme 5).9
Scheme 5
6 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 2,3-Dieneni-
triles
Hydrohalogenation of 2,3-butadienenitrile 18a with MX
in HOAc afforded the corresponding 3- halo-3-buteneni-
triles with yields ranging from 78% to 86%. However, the
hydrohalogenation of 4-methyl-2,3-pentadienenitrile 18b
with MX in HOAc afforded the corresponding 3-halo-4-
methyl-3-pentenenitriles in low yields (17-37%). When a
1:1 mixture of CF
3CO2H and HOAc was used as the reac-
tion medium, the hydrohalogenation went smoothly to af-
ford 3-halo-4-methyl-3-pentenenitriles in fairly good
yields (76-80%) and excellent selectivities. The corre-
sponding reactions with 2,3-octadienenitrile 18c or 4-phe-
nyl-2,3-butadienenitrile 18d also went smoothly to afford
4-substitutied 3-halo-3-alkenenitriles 19 with yields rang-
ing from 37% to 82% (Scheme 6), and 4-phenyl-2,3-buta-
dienenitrile 18d only afforded the E-isomer due to the
existence of the phenyl group.
Scheme 6
7 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1, 2-Allenic 
Sulfones
Three sets of reaction conditions were established to carry
out the hydrohalogenation reactions of 1,2-allenic sul-
fones 20 with metallic halides (Scheme 7).

yields ranging from 67-80%, and the reaction of HX (con-
ditions C) with 1,2-allenic sulfones also afforded the hy-
drohalogenation products in reasonable yields (65-83%).
The migration of the C=C bond in product 21 was not ob-
served even when 21 was heated in HOAc at 118 °C for
11 h.

8 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1, 2-Allenic 
Sulfoxides
Hydrohalogenation reactions of 1,2-allenic sulfoxides
with MX in HOAc failed to provide the expected 2-ha-
loallylic sulfoxides (Scheme 8), probably due to the fol-
lowing two reasons: (1) the electron-withdrawing ability
of sulfinyl group (RSO) is much weaker than that of sul-
fonyl group (RSO
2),15 and (2) allenic sulfoxides are rela-
tively unstable in acidic media such as HX at moderate
temperature (50-70 °C).
16 
Scheme 8
After screening over numerous reaction conditions, AlCl3
was found to show obvious activity, and a certain amount
of water promoted this reaction. The ratio of AlCl
3 and
H2O has big influence on the speed of this conversion and
the reaction with 0.55 equiv. of AlCl3 and 1 equiv. of wa-
ter are the most efficient.17
Under the reaction conditions, hydrohalogenation reac-
tions of 1,2-allenic sulfoxides with AlBr
3 or AlCl3 afford-
ed the corresponding 2-haloallylic sulfoxides with yields
ranging from 56% to 89%. The reaction with AlBr 3 was
less efficient than the hydrochlorination reaction with
AlCl
3. The structure of allenic sulfoxide is important: the
reaction of some allenic sulfoxides, i.e. 22e, 22f and 22g,
did not proceed, probably due to the steric hindrance of
the allenic sulfoxides. The hydrohalogenation yields for
22a (81-89%) are usually higher than that for 22b (64-
71%), probably due to the higher stability of 22a in the re-
action media, since the control experiment showed that
the reaction of 22b was faster than that of 22a (Scheme
9).
17
Scheme 9
Hydroiodination can be realized by using a combination
of AlCl
3 and NaI (Scheme 10). When 4 equiv. of NaI and
0.55 equiv. of AlCl 3 were used, we did not observe the
formation of any hydrochlorination product. However
when we used 1 equiv. of 22a, 1 equiv. of NaI, and 0.55
equiv. of AlCl
3, 20% of the hydrochlorination product
was formed together with the hydroiodination product.
The hydroiodination reaction of PhS(O)CH=C=CHCH
3
(22c) afforded the corresponding 2-iodoallyl sulfoxide  in
an isomeric Z/E ratio of 92: 8.17
Scheme 10
The mechanism of this reaction is the Al(III)-mediated
nucleophilic attack of X- at the center carbon atom of the
electron-deficient allenes.
9 Hydrohalogenation Reaction of 1,2-Allenic 
Diphenylphosphine Oxides
Hydrohalogenation reactions of propadienyl diphe-
nylphosphine oxide 24a w i t h  M X  ( M = N a ,  L i ,  X = C l ,
Br, I) in HOAc afforded 2-halo-2-propenyl diphenylphos-
phine oxides 25 in reasonable yields, ranging from 58% to
75%, while the similar reaction with aqueous HX afforded
the products in much lower yields (31-46%). However, in
cases of 24b and 24c, the reactivities towards MX in
HOAc were low (Scheme 11).

11 Conclusion
We have developed a convenient methodology for the
synthesis of 1-functionalized 2-halo-2-alkenes, such as
2-halo-2-alkenyl ketones, carboxylic acids, esters,
amides, nitriles, sulfoxides (mediated by AlX
3), sulfones,
and phosphine oxides via the simple reaction of electron-
deficient allenes with MX in HOAc, CF
3CO2H-HOAc,
CF3CO2H CF3CO2H or THF. In most cases, the yields are
high; the stereoselectivity depends on the reaction temper-
ature and the solvent used; the ratios of /c98/c44/c103-unsaturated
and /c97/c44/c98-unsaturated products are determined by the acid-
ity of solvent used. The uniquely located C=C bonds, C-
X bonds, and the electron-withdrawing functional groups
make these products synthetically useful. In most cases,
the Z- and E-isomers can be readily separated providing
efficient entries to both relevent stereoisomers.
